title: O, Richly, Father, Have I Been
description: O, Richly, Father, Have I Been in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Furness wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 203, “The Penitent Son”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, rich-ly, Fa-ther, have I been Blest ev-er-more by Thee! And morn-ing, noon, and night Thou hast Pre-served me ten-der-ly.

lines: O, richly, Father, have I been
Blest evermore by Thee!
And morning, noon, and night Thou hast
Preserved me tenderly.
And yet the love which Thou shouldst claim
To idols I have given;
Too oft have bound to earth the hopes
That know no home but heaven.
Unworthy to be called Thy son,
I come with shame to Thee,
Father! — O, more than Father, Thou
Hast always been to me!
Help me to break the heavy chains
The world has round me thrown,
And know the glorious liberty
Of an obedient son.
That I may henceforth heed whate'er
Thy voice within me saith,
Fix deeply in my heart of hearts
A principle of faith, —
Faith that, like armor to my soul,
Shall keep all evil out,
More mighty than an angel host,
Encamping round about.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Henry Furness died in 1896.
credits: Words by William Henry Furness (1802–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
